title: The Silicon Heartland Wants To Be America’s Next Chip Powerhouse
gist: A wave of Midwestern semiconductor investment — Intel's $28B+ Ohio fabs, SK hynix's >$4B West Lafayette HBM packaging hub, Hemlock's polysilicon expansion, and a multi-billion-dollar Chicago quantum park anchored by PsiQuantum — is turning the region into a candidate ecosystem rather than a set of isolated projects. Whether it becomes durable hinges on two constraints: training technicians and process engineers faster than any prior regional initiative, and getting private capital to deploy on organic demand rather than on government funding cycles.

themes.theme: Anchor fab and packaging capex in the Midwest

insights.claim: Intel's "Silicon Heartland" project in New Albany, suburban Central Ohio, is a $28B+ leading-edge wafer fabrication investment expected to open in the early 2030s and to create 3,000 new Intel jobs in the Columbus metro area once fully operational.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Sizes the single largest anchor tenant of a new U.S. fab cluster and the labor demand that suppliers and staffing around Columbus will have to absorb.
insights.quote: One of the biggest markers of the industry’s Midwestern development has been Intel’s $28B+ “Silicon Heartland” project in suburban Central Ohio.
insights.locator: Defining the Midwestern ecosystem

insights.claim: Intel's Ohio One Fab 1 and Fab 2 are in active construction on a schedule extended from Intel's original plan, with first fab operations targeted around 2030-31 and second fab operations around 2032.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: The multi-year slip means revenue and local supplier pull-through from Ohio arrives late this decade at the earliest, not in the current CHIPS-era news cycle.
insights.quote: Active construction; schedule extended from Intel’s original plan.
insights.locator: Major Midwest Semiconductor Activities table, Ohio row

insights.claim: SK hynix broke ground on Aug. 27, 2026 on a more than $4B HBM advanced packaging, testing and R&D hub in West Lafayette, Indiana — described as the first U.S. HBM advanced packaging and test facility — with cleanroom targeted for Oct. 2028 and mass production in H2 2029.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Puts a piece of the AI memory supply chain's back end on U.S. soil for the first time, on a timeline that matters for late-decade AI accelerator sourcing.
insights.quote: Broke ground Aug. 27, 2026. First U.S. HBM advanced packaging and test facility.
insights.locator: Major Midwest Semiconductor Activities table, Indiana row

insights.claim: Hemlock Semiconductor is building a new semiconductor-grade hyper-pure polysilicon facility in Thomas Township, Michigan with roughly $825M expected capex and a CHIPS award of up to $325M, targeting production in 2028.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Domestic hyper-pure polysilicon is an upstream chokepoint; a 2028 start date defines when U.S. wafer feedstock independence actually improves.
insights.quote: New semiconductor-grade polysilicon manufacturing facility supported by finalized CHIPS incentives.
insights.locator: Major Midwest Semiconductor Activities table, Michigan row

insights.claim: Polar Semiconductor is spending more than $525M to expand and modernize its Bloomington, Minnesota 200-mm fab for power, sensor and high-voltage devices, intending to nearly double production and adding GaN-on-Si manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Shows the Midwest build-out is not only leading-edge logic — domestic power and GaN capacity serves automotive and industrial demand on a nearer timeline.
insights.quote: Fab expansion and modernization intended to nearly double production; GaN-on-Si manufacturing added.
insights.locator: Major Midwest Semiconductor Activities table, Minnesota row

insights.claim: NHanced Semiconductors' Odon, Indiana advanced-packaging facility for 2.5D/3D packaging, chiplets, hybrid bonding and photonics is operational, but its Bloomington expansion was canceled in May 2024 and the company was acquired by Quantum Computing Inc. in June 2026, with Indiana operations continuing under QCi ownership.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: A cautionary datapoint: regional packaging plans get canceled and small players get absorbed, so announced project pipelines overstate realized capacity.
insights.quote: Bloomington expansion canceled in May 2024. Acquired by Quantum Computing Inc. in June 2026; Indiana operations continuing under QCi ownership.
insights.locator: Major Midwest Semiconductor Activities table, Indiana/NHanced row

themes.theme: Ecosystem thesis: integration with industrial base, not design-only clustering

insights.claim: A regional cluster becomes an ecosystem only when supply-chain building blocks — water treatment capabilities, semiconductor tools, and material growth development — can connect to each other locally rather than being sourced from the coasts.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Gives investors a concrete test for whether a subsidized fab site is generating durable supplier revenue or just a standalone plant.
insights.quote: So the building blocks for semiconductor work can connect within that Midwest ecosystem through additional supply chain capabilities.
insights.locator: Defining the Midwestern ecosystem — Casto quote

insights.claim: The Midwest's differentiating strategy is to tie semiconductor innovation directly to manufacturing and industrial end markets — automotive technology, defense applications, and research institutions — rather than concentrating in either design or fabrication as other regions have.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Implies the region's chip demand and differentiation come from industrial/auto/defense integration, a different cycle exposure than a design-hub model.
insights.quote: While some regions are heavily concentrated in either semiconductor design or fabrication, the Midwest is building a more integrated ecosystem
insights.locator: Defining the Midwestern ecosystem — Salomone quote

insights.claim: A "materials corridor" is forming across the Midwest that did not exist five years ago, built by deliberate geographic deepening — Brewer Science's footprint running from Rolla to Vichy to Springfield and now Dayton, Ohio via its acquisition of Heraeus Epurio's semiconductor chemicals business.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: M&A of specialty chemical assets, not greenfield fabs, is how the materials layer of a regional cluster actually gets assembled — a pattern to watch for further deals.
insights.quote: you start to see a materials corridor forming across the Midwest that didn’t exist five years ago
insights.locator: Defining the Midwestern ecosystem — Kommu quote

insights.claim: Brewer Science's presence in the Midwest since 1981 is offered as evidence that world-class materials innovation and manufacturing can thrive outside traditional coastal hubs, directly challenging the historical consolidation of semiconductor ecosystems.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Undercuts the default assumption that semiconductor agglomeration economics force coastal or Asian concentration.
insights.quote: Brewer Science has been rooted in the Midwest since 1981, and our positioning isn’t incidental to the region; it’s strategic
insights.locator: Defining the Midwestern ecosystem — Kommu quote

insights.claim: The manufacturers that will matter most in the region are those treating it as a 20-year investment in institutional capability rather than a response to quarterly performance metrics.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: A screening heuristic: suppliers managing to quarterly metrics are unlikely to hold the regional positions that pay off late this decade.
insights.quote: The manufacturers who will matter most in this region are those treating this as a 20-year investment in institutional capability, not a response to quarterly performance metrics.
insights.locator: Defining the Midwestern ecosystem — Kommu quote

themes.theme: Workforce velocity and capital durability as the binding constraints

insights.claim: Two challenges determine whether the regional semiconductor resurgence becomes durable: workforce velocity and capital market confidence.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: A compact two-variable frame for underwriting regional chip clusters that cuts past headline capex announcements.
insights.quote: Two challenges will determine whether this regional resurgence becomes durable: workforce velocity and capital market confidence.
insights.locator: Filling the gaps in workforce development and funding

insights.claim: The region must train technicians, process engineers and materials scientists faster than any regional initiative has previously managed, and doing so requires a 10-to-15-year commitment to community college partnerships, apprenticeships and industry-sponsored training with uncertain ROI.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Labor, not fab construction, is the realistic gating item on Midwest ramp schedules — and its payback period exceeds most corporate planning horizons.
insights.quote: The Midwest needs to train and develop technicians, process engineers, and materials scientists faster than any regional initiative has previously managed
insights.locator: Filling the gaps in workforce development and funding

insights.claim: If private sector growth follows the funding cycles of government initiatives rather than organic market demand, the region risks boom-bust dynamics that damage competitiveness, making self-sustaining business models rather than ongoing subsidy dependence the real test.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Flags subsidy-cycle correlation as a specific risk factor for suppliers whose backlog is tied to government-funded projects.
insights.quote: If private sector growth follows the funding cycles of government initiatives, rather than organic market demand, the region risks boom-bust dynamics that damage competitiveness.
insights.locator: Filling the gaps in workforce development and funding

insights.claim: The Midwest has historically produced exceptional engineers and researchers who then built their careers elsewhere, and the new investment's real effect is giving graduates a visible in-region pathway into leading-edge semiconductor manufacturing.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Reversing brain drain is the mechanism by which fab capex converts into a durable local talent base — and the metric that would confirm the thesis.
insights.quote: Too often, however, many of those graduates built their careers elsewhere.
insights.locator: Defining the Midwestern ecosystem — Geer quote

insights.claim: Brewer Science became a Certified Employee-Owned company in 2020 explicitly as a retention lever in a tight technical labor market, and chose to deepen its Midwest footprint rather than chasing the lowest-cost location.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: An unconventional ownership structure is being used as competitive HR capital in a sector where technician attrition throttles fab ramps.
insights.quote: We became a Certified Employee-Owned company in 2020, which means the people doing the work also have a direct stake in the company’s success.
insights.locator: Filling the gaps in workforce development and funding

insights.claim: The open question for the region is how effectively today's public and private investments translate into a durable ecosystem that stays globally competitive over the next decade, which depends on sustained industry-academia-government collaboration plus supply chain security.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Frames the investment case as a decade-long execution question rather than a build-announcement event.
insights.locator: Filling the gaps in workforce development and funding — Salomone quote

themes.theme: Chicago quantum cluster as the region's open-field bet

insights.claim: The Chicagoland quantum push is backed by $500 million in Illinois state funding for the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park plus a planned $1 billion investment from PsiQuantum, on part of the former U.S. Steel South Works site on Chicago's south side lakefront.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Quantifies one of the largest subnational quantum commitments in the U.S. and identifies PsiQuantum as its anchor private counterparty.
insights.quote: with $500 million in Illinois state funding for the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park and a planned $1 billion investment from PsiQuantum
insights.locator: Quantum opportunities

insights.claim: The University of Chicago-affiliated Chicago Quantum Exchange projects emerging quantum technology could generate up to $80B in economic impact for Illinois, Wisconsin and Indiana by 2035.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: An explicit, datable size estimate for tri-state quantum economic impact that can be tested against actual commercialization by 2035.
insights.quote: could generate up to $80B in economic impact for Illinois, Wisconsin, and Indiana by 2035
insights.locator: Quantum opportunities

insights.claim: The region's advantage in quantum depends on continuing to launch initiatives 18 to 24 months ahead of other regions, an edge the Midwest has not typically maintained in other sectors.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Gives a measurable lead-time metric for judging whether the Chicago cluster is holding or losing its position.
insights.quote: If the Midwest keeps its foot on the pedal and continues launching initiatives 18 to 24 months ahead of others, the region can maintain its advantage
insights.locator: Quantum opportunities — Timmerman quote

insights.claim: Most industries are already mature enough that the Midwest could not realistically become a top-two ecosystem in them, but quantum is still open — which is why it is the region's most winnable category.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: A clear-eyed admission that regional catch-up only works in immature technology categories — useful for pricing regional cluster claims elsewhere.
insights.quote: Many industries are already mature enough that it would be difficult for the Midwest to become a top two ecosystem, but quantum is still open.
insights.locator: Quantum opportunities — Timmerman quote

insights.claim: The Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park is designed to house companies including IBM and PsiQuantum working on chips, silicon photonics and quantum hardware for pharma, chemistry, energy and defense applications.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Names the tenant roster and end markets that would monetize the site, including silicon photonics — a bridge between quantum and mainstream chip supply chains.
insights.locator: Quantum opportunities

insights.claim: The quantum supply chain spans materials, components, subsystems and full systems, and regional manufacturers already produce inputs such as diamond, vacuum systems and nanopositioners that could scale into a domestic quantum supply chain that does not yet fully exist.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Points to unglamorous component vendors — not qubit startups — as the near-term investable layer of quantum.
insights.quote: We already have regional manufacturers producing materials such as diamond, as well as components such as vacuum systems and nanopositioners.
insights.locator: Quantum opportunities — Timmerman quote for manufacturers

insights.claim: Quantum sensors are already at relatively high technology-readiness levels and can be bought and piloted today, while quantum networking and quantum computing remain farther off.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Separates the near-term revenue segment of quantum from the long-dated ones — sensing is where commercial orders exist now.
insights.quote: Quantum sensors are already at relatively high technology-readiness levels, and companies can buy and pilot systems today.
insights.locator: Quantum opportunities — Timmerman, for end users

insights.claim: Even though quantum systems require fundamentally different architectures than conventional computing, they still rely on sophisticated design methodologies, simulation technologies and increasingly complex semiconductor components — creating an EDA and modeling attach point.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: EDA vendors have a credible, non-speculative revenue path into quantum via design, modeling and verification rather than qubit technology bets.
insights.quote: While quantum systems require fundamentally different architectures than conventional computing, they still rely on sophisticated design methodologies, simulation technologies, and increasingly complex semiconductor components.
insights.locator: Quantum opportunities — Salomone quote

insights.claim: The Duality Accelerator, launched in 2020-2021 as the first quantum-focused startup accelerator in the U.S. and managed by the Chicago Quantum Exchange, has supported roughly 25 to 30 startups across quantum computing, communications, sensing and enabling technologies, with companies like qBraid relocating to the region.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete deal-flow count for the region's quantum startup pipeline and evidence that infrastructure access pulls companies to relocate.
insights.quote: To date, Duality has supported roughly 25 to 30 startups.
insights.locator: Quantum opportunities — Timmerman on Duality

themes.theme: Startup infrastructure economics and the Valley of Death

insights.claim: The Midwest Microelectronics Consortium's core role is helping regional entrepreneurs survive the "Valley of Death" by giving members access to compute environments, design tools and prototyping capabilities at lower cost or through different cost models than were previously available.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Shared-infrastructure consortia, not venture capital alone, are the mechanism lowering the entry cost for hardware startups outside coastal hubs.
insights.quote: Streamlining access to prototyping capabilities, whether that be tools to do epitaxial development, or the ability to do advanced packaging and module development and characterization and tests
insights.locator: Startup support — Casto quote

insights.claim: MMEC is developing intellectual property and building startup design feedback into its digital infrastructure specifically to make it easier for other companies to use foundry ecosystems, aggregating requirements to lower costs through economies of scale.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: Demand aggregation by a consortium is a non-obvious lever for reducing per-startup foundry access cost, and a potential channel partner for EDA and IP vendors.
insights.quote: We can aggregate requirements and lower costs through economies of scale for other businesses to use.
insights.locator: Startup support — Casto quote

insights.claim: EDA companies historically supplied tools to universities in order to hire graduates and relocate them to existing tech hubs; what has changed is that new jobs are now being created outside those hubs, where cost of living is far lower than in places like Silicon Valley.
insights.speaker: Brendan Heffernan
insights.so_what: A structural shift in engineering labor geography that lowers the wage base for chip design work and changes where EDA seat growth lands.
insights.quote: in the past the goal was to hire new engineering graduates and relocate them back to existing tech hubs
insights.locator: Startup support
